1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e3 c5 5.Bd3.strategy: The flexible developing move: it covers d4 and e5 and lets White meet ...Bxc3 with the bishop pair and doubled c-pawns, without a tempo spent on a3. White bets that the two bishops and the centre outweigh the weak queenside pawns once the position opens.

Asks the bishop to decide at once, but Black was ready to take on c3 anyway. White gets the bishop pair and doubled c-pawns for a tempo spent on the a-pawn while the kingside is still undeveloped, so Black has time to set up a blockade.
Takes the knight and doubles White's pawns, the usual aim of the pin. Black gives up the bishop pair for a lasting queenside weakness and keeps the pressure on d4 with the c-pawn and the knight.

Captures at once, without waiting for a3. Black then closes the centre and blockades the dark squares, so that the knights outplay White's bishops and the doubled c-pawns leave White without pawn breaks on the queenside.
